mainTopic: When a dead נזיר's money, animals, or other items set aside for his offerings count as specified (מפורשין) or unspecified (סתומין), and whether the rule applies only to coins.
overview: If a נזיר dies after setting aside money for his three offerings (חטאת, עולה, שלמים), the outcome depends on whether the money was specified (מפורשין) for each offering or left unspecified (סתומין). The amud opens with a ברייתא that supports רבא for cases where only one offering was specified. If the חטאת money was specified, it is destroyed, and the rest is split between an עולה and a שלמים. If only the עולה money was specified, the rest goes to נדבה. רב הונא in the name of רב teaches that the specified-or-unspecified distinction applies only to money, because an animal shows by its kind which offering it is for. רב נחמן limits this to unblemished animals and says a silver bar counts as specified. רב נחמן בר יצחק disagrees: a silver bar is like money, and only a pile of beams counts as specified. רב שימי בר אשי then asks why the rule should be limited to coins. רב חסדא treats pairs of birds as unspecified until the owner or the כהן assigns them, so the rule seems to reach beyond money. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא: the sin-offering money was specified
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא matches רבא's view. If a נזיר specified money for his חטאת and left the rest general, the חטאת money is destroyed, and the rest is split between an עולה and a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רבא: If a נזיר said, "This money is for my sin-offering, and the rest is for the rest of my נזירות offerings," and then died, the sin-offering money is thrown into the Dead Sea. With the rest, half goes to a burnt-offering and half to a peace-offering. Someone who uses all of it commits מעילה, but someone who uses only part of it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רבא. It shows how to handle a dead נזיר's money when he specified only the sin-offering portion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the חטאת money has been separated out, the rest can only be for the עולה and the שלמים, so it is treated as known and divided between them. Spending all of it surely includes some עולה money, which is holy, so there is מעילה. Spending only part might take only שלמים money, so there is no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with him
Money set aside for a sin-offering
The Dead Sea, meaning the money is destroyed and no one benefits from it
One is liable for מְעִילָה, misusing holy property
With only part of them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rest is unspecified money that goes to נדבה. Because the חטאת money was already removed, the rest is split between the עולה and the שלמים.

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in accordance with רבא:
"This money is for my sin-offering
phrases.notes: The case is a נזיר who set aside this money and then died before bringing his offerings.

phrases.english: and the rest is for the rest of my nazirite offerings,"
the sin-offering money is cast into the Dead Sea,
and the rest: he brings half of it for a burnt-offering
and half of it for a peace-offering.
And one is liable for misuse with all of it,
but one is not liable for misuse with part of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's ruling, which the גמרא discussed just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view on partly specified נזיר money
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about money specified for the חטאת, with the rest left for the other offerings

steps.title: Second case of the ברייתא: the burnt-offering money was specified
steps.stepSummary: If the נזיר specified only the עולה money, it is brought as an עולה, and the rest goes to communal gift offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, "This is for my burnt-offering, and the rest is for the rest of my נזירות offerings," the burnt-offering money is used to bring a burnt-offering, and someone who uses it commits מעילה. The rest goes to gift offerings (נדבה). Someone who uses all of it commits מעילה, but someone who uses only part of it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the opposite case. Here only the burnt-offering portion was specified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The specified עולה money is simply used for an עולה. The rest still has the חטאת money mixed in with the שלמים money, so it cannot be split up. It goes to נדבה, like unspecified money. The rule about using all of it versus part of it is the same as in the first case.

keyTerms.meaning: Money set aside for a burnt-offering
It goes to the fund for communal gift offerings

steps.whatToRemember: Whether the remainder can be divided depends on which offering was taken out. If the חטאת is removed, the rest is split between the עולה and the שלמים. If only the עולה is removed, the rest still contains חטאת money and goes to נדבה.

phrases.english: "This money is for my burnt-offering
and the rest is for the rest of my nazirite offerings,"
the burnt-offering money: they bring a burnt-offering with it,
and one is liable for misuse with it.
And the rest goes to gift offerings,
and one is liable for misuse with all of it,
but one is not liable for misuse with part of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the parallel case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second clause of the same ברייתא

steps.title: An animal counts as specified
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא in the name of רב: the difference between specified and unspecified applies only to money. A designated animal is automatically treated as specified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: They taught this only about money. An animal, however, is treated as specified.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching limits the whole topic of unspecified funds to money. Animals are treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר's three offerings are different kinds of animals: a female lamb for the חטאת, a male lamb for the עולה, and a ram for the שלמים. So the animal itself shows which offering it is for, even if he never said so. Each animal is then handled as a specified offering.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only about
Money
As if specified for a particular offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next step, where רב נחמן puts a limit on this rule.

phrases.english: רב הונא said that רב said:
They taught this only about money,
but an animal is treated as specified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new point that limits the specified versus unspecified rules to money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A designated animal is treated as specified, so the specified-or-unspecified question applies only to money.

steps.title: Only an unblemished animal counts as specified
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן limits רב's rule: only an unblemished animal counts as specified. A blemished animal is treated like unspecified money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The rule that an animal is treated as specified was taught only about an unblemished animal. A blemished animal, however, is treated as unspecified.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן narrows the previous rule. It applies only to animals that can actually be brought as offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished animal cannot be offered. It will be sold, and only its money will be used. So even if it is the right kind of animal, it is really just a stand-in for money, and it is treated like unspecified money.

keyTerms.meaning: Unblemished, fit to be offered
A blemished animal
As if unspecified

phrases.english: רב נחמן said:
That which they say, that an animal
is treated as specified,
they taught this only about an unblemished one,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בַּעֲלַת מוּם — הֲרֵי הִיא כִּסְתוּמָה.
phrases.english: but a blemished one is treated as unspecified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הָא דְּאָמְרִי בְּהֵמָה הֲרֵי הִיא כִּמְפוֹרֶשֶׁת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only an unblemished animal counts as specified. A blemished animal is treated as unspecified.

steps.title: A silver bar is not like a blemished animal
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן adds that a bar of silver is not treated as unspecified.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a bar of silver is not treated that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן finishes with a short exception. A silver bar does not follow the rule of the blemished animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like a blemished animal, a silver bar will also be turned into money. Even so, each bar is a separate, distinct item set aside for a particular offering, so it counts as specified.

keyTerms.meaning: A bar or ingot of silver

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, coins and a blemished animal can be unspecified. An unblemished animal and a separate silver bar count as specified. The next step shows that רב נחמן בר יצחק disagrees about the silver bar.

phrases.english: But a silver bar is not treated that way.
phrases.notes: "That way" means as unspecified money. Each bar counts as set aside for its own offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends רב נחמן's statement by setting a silver bar apart from a blemished animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bar of silver set aside for an offering is treated as specified, not as unspecified.

steps.title: Even a silver bar counts as unspecified, but a pile of beams does not
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק disagrees with רב נחמן. He says a silver bar is treated like unspecified money, but a pile of beams is treated as specified.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Even a silver bar is treated like unspecified money. But a pile of beams is not.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא draws the line in a different place. For him, a silver bar works like unspecified coins, and only something like a pile of beams is treated as specified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רב נחמן said a silver bar is NOT like unspecified money. רב נחמן בר יצחק disagrees and puts the silver bar together with coins. He moves the cut-off point to building beams, which are clearly not money at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A bar or ingot of silver
A pile or stack
Beams, wooden building beams

phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Even a silver bar,
phrases.notes: He means even a silver bar counts as unspecified money, which is the opposite of what רב נחמן said in the last step.

phrases.english: but a pile of beams — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ נְסָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב נחמן's ruling on a silver bar and sets a wider boundary for unspecified money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A silver bar is treated as unspecified money; a pile of beams is treated as specified.

steps.title: If only coins count, birds should not count either
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי asks רב פפא what the reasoning is for limiting the rule to coins and excluding animals, silver bars, and beams. If that is the reasoning, birds should be excluded too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said to רב פפא: What is the reasoning of these רבנן who say that the rule is for coins and not an animal or a silver bar, and for coins and not a pile? If so, it should also be for coins and not birds!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי questions the whole idea of the last few statements. He says that if the rule is only for coins, then birds should be excluded too, and he is preparing to show why that is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב, רב נחמן, and רב נחמן בר יצחק all seem to assume that the rule of unspecified funds was taught only for coins. רב שימי pushes that logic further: anything that is not coins, including birds, should then be excluded. This sets up the attack in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their reasoning?
But if so, then... (pushing an idea to its logical result)
Birds

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said to Rav Pappa:
What is the reasoning of the Rabbis, who say:
phrases.notes: "The Rabbis" here means the אמוראים from the last few steps: רב, רב נחמן, and רב נחמן בר יצחק.

phrases.english: money, and not an animal and not a silver bar,
money and not a pile?
But if so: money and not birds!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי לְרַב פָּפָּא: מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the shared assumption behind steps 3 through 6 that the rule applies only to coins.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רב, רב נחמן, and רב נחמן בר יצחק that the rule of unspecified funds is limited to coins.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule is limited to coins, then birds should also never be treated as unspecified. The next step shows that this result does not fit רב חסדא's ruling.

steps.title: רב חסדא treats birds as unspecified, so the rule is not only for coins
steps.stepSummary: Someone might answer that birds really are excluded. But רב חסדא says a pair of birds becomes assigned only when the owner buys them for a purpose or when the כהן offers them. So birds can be unspecified, which should not be possible if the rule is only for coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: Yes, that is so, birds are excluded. But what about what רב חסדא said: A pair of birds becomes assigned only when the owners buy them for a purpose, or when the כהן offers them. Why should that be? We learned this rule only for money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible way out: you might simply accept that birds are excluded. Then it quotes רב חסדא, who treats birds as unspecified, and asks why, if the rule was learned only for coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא says unassigned birds stay unspecified until the owner or the כהן decides which bird is for which קרבן. That means the idea of 'unspecified' does apply to something besides coins. If birds are included, there seems to be no good reason to exclude animals, silver bars, or beams.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: yes, that is indeed so
Pairs of birds (turtledoves or young pigeons), one for an עולה and one for a חטאת
Become specified, assigned to a particular קרבן
The owner's purchase, when the owner assigns each bird as he buys it
The כהן's act of offering, when he decides which bird is for which קרבן
We learned it as a received tradition

steps.whatToRemember: The question is not yet answered: רב חסדא's ruling on birds shows that 'unspecified' can apply beyond coins. That weakens the reason for excluding animals, silver bars, and beams.
steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not discussing a נזיר. His ruling about birds is brought only to show that the idea of 'unspecified' is not limited to coins.

phrases.english: And if you will say: So too,
phrases.notes: In other words, you might simply agree that birds can never be unspecified.

phrases.english: but what about this that Rav Ḥisda said:
Pairs of birds do not become specified,
except either by the owner's purchase,
or by the priest's action.
Why? We learned it only about money!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב שימי בר אשי's challenge by blocking the answer 'birds are excluded' with רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the rule of unspecified funds applies only to coins.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא treats unassigned birds as unspecified. That extends the rule beyond coins, so excluding animals, silver bars, and beams seems to have no basis.
